chunks: Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ narrated from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a matter concerning which Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Qummī al-Ashʿarī had written to me. He said: We have estates in which there are fire temples, to which the Magians bring cattle, sheep, and dirhams. Is it permissible for the owners of the villages to take that, while the fire temples have caretakers who oversee them?
Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام said: “Let the owners of the villages take from that; there is no harm in it.”

key_terms.أَرْبَابِ الْقُرَى: the owners or proprietors of the villages
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it; it is permissible
key_terms.قُوَّامٌ: caretakers or attendants who manage something
key_terms.مَسْأَلَةٍ: a legal question or matter requiring a ruling

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take offerings given by the Magians to fire temples located on one's land?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal question posed to Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام regarding offerings made by the Magians to fire temples located on village lands. The Imam rules that the owners of the villages may take such items, and that there is no harm in doing so.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.4082 - Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' narrated from Imam Ali ibn Musa Ar-Ridha (as):
I asked him about a question that Muhammad ibn Abdullah al-Qummi al-Ash'ari had written to me.
He said: "We have lands where there are fire temples, and the Magians (Majus) offer cattle, sheep, and dirhams as gifts to these temples. Is it permissible for the landowners to take these offerings, knowing that the fire temples have caretakers who oversee them?"
Abu al-Hasan (as) said: "The landowners may take them, and there is no harm in it."
